label: [ K-IG 교육 Reading 122 ]

blocks.text: In the early 1990s, Colombia earned much less money from its exports than it had before. Its major export crop was coffee, and in 1989 an international agreement that had helped keep coffee prices high came to an end. At the same time, other countries were exporting more coffee, so there was more coffee on the world market than buyers needed. As a result, coffee prices fell to their lowest level in years. Because of these factors, Colombia got much less cash from its coffee exports.
